# Adhd Care

This folder contains the complete set of national clinical quality indicators used to monitor and evaluate ADHD care in Denmark, managed by the ADHD-DATABASEN. It covers both process and result indicators across the assessment and treatment populations, tracking critical milestones such as somatic evaluations, diagnostic conferences, cross-sectoral coordination, psychoeducation, and pharmacological treatments for children, adolescents, and adults. The pages detail the specific targets, regional disparities, and systemic shortfalls for each metric, highlighting ongoing challenges in meeting the established 90% development goals and the structural revisions undertaken by the steering committee to improve data registration and clinical practice.

## Pages

- [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] — Tracks the completion of somatic assessments within 120 days of starting an ADHD evaluation, revealing national averages well below the 90% target.
- [[indikator-10|Indikator 10]] — Tracks the assessment of social support needs for adults within 120 days of treatment start, heavily impacted by data registration practices rather than clinical omissions.
- [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]] — Monitors the initiation of pharmacological treatment for adults within 120 days of starting a package course, revealing significant regional registration disparities.
- [[indikator-2a|Indikator 2a]] — Measures the use of clinical environmental observations within 120 days for children aged 0–5 undergoing ADHD assessment.
- [[indikator-2b|Indikator 2b]] — Evaluates the application of manualized diagnostic interviews or environmental observations for youth aged 6–17, currently undergoing structural revision to separate distinct assessment elements.
- [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] — Monitors the holding of diagnostic conferences with a child and adolescent psychiatry specialist within 120 days, highlighting severe systemic shortfalls and regional disparities.
- [[indikator-4|Indikator 4]] — Tracks cross-sectoral coordination, recently revised from a treatment metric to an assessment indicator requiring contact with the patient's home municipality within 120 days.
- [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] — Measures the initiation of ADHD-related psychoeducation for patients or parents within 120 days of treatment start, consistently falling far below the 90% standard.
- [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] — Records the proportion of treatment pathways where patients receive pharmacological ADHD treatment, showing relatively higher national compliance rates around 62–68%.
- [[indikator-7a|Indikator 7a]] — A result indicator tracking the proportion of youth in the ADHD assessment population who pass the primary school leaving exam before turning 17.
- [[indikator-7b|Indikator 7b]] — A comparative result indicator measuring the same primary school exam milestone specifically for youth in the ADHD treatment population.
- [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] — Evaluates the initiation of ADHD-related psychoeducation for adult patients within 120 days of treatment, reported for the first time in 2024/25 with a 36% national average.
- [[indikator-9|Indikator 9]] — Measures the provision of relevant psychotherapy to adults within one year of treatment initiation, exposing a severe systemic shortfall with just 1% national compliance.
